title: Worker briefs and gate questions give measured figures with the command that measured them, and the sprint reviewer runs in a worktree of its own
goal: Retrospective of SP-vayhvwfy: ST-icgtdnuf's worker modelled the worker worktree name on the brief's example agent-ST-xxxxxxxx, and the operator confirmed gate g1 (limit 179) on it, while Agent-tool worktrees here are agent-<17 hex>, 6 characters longer (parked ST-6xdymgtg); and the fresh-context reviewer, started in the orchestrator's checkout, had its SessionStart intake hook file drafts there, which made one landing refuse a dirty tree. The kb-sprint skill's brief parts say a figure a worker or a gate relies on is measured (with its command) rather than given as an example, and the review step starts the reviewer in a worktree or scratch checkout of its own, names its launch (--max-turns, its cwd and scratch directory, read-only) and runs the whole tests.py only after the reviewer has returned, since a concurrent run took 21 s against the 20 s darwin ceiling (SP-rvslem3h).

run: import sys;t=open(".claude/skills/kb-sprint/SKILL.md",encoding="utf-8").read();r=t.split("## review SP")[1].split("## close SP")[0];a="worktree of its own" in r and "--max-turns" in r and "read-only" in r;b="measured" in t and "command" in t;print("review step 4 names the reviewer launch:",a,"; briefs ask for measured figures:",b);sys.exit(0 if a and b else 1)

gates.question: Where does the sprint's fresh-context reviewer run?
options: a git worktree of its own under .claude/worktrees, as a worker's
gates.recommendation: a git worktree of its own under .claude/worktrees, as a worker's
gates.answer: a git worktree of its own under .claude/worktrees, as a worker's
